messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1851234567 - Elevated error rate + unexpected telemetry exporter enabled in us-west-2 inference pool. Pager: @jamie (oncall). See runbook: <https://redwood-internal/runbooks/inference-triage>
jamie (oncall): oncall here, looking. Paging eng-sre: @alex. Pulling logs now.
alex (eng-sre): quick heads-up — initial grep shows a config flip for `telemetry.debug_export=true` at 04:12:05 UTC. Export target: telemetry-prod S3 (internal). I can see a handful of payloads with a field `debug_preview` that includes the first ~128 chars of requests when the flag is on.
alex (eng-sre): sample (redacted):
```json
{"client_id_hash":"sha256:****","model":"rwd-2b","debug_preview":"Customer prompt: \"How to implement a feature flag that...\" (truncated)"}
```
jamie (oncall): ok — do we have PII or API keys in those previews?
alex (eng-sre): no full API keys. Looks like only the prompt prefix and a client identifier hash. The preview sometimes contains user-provided text (could be PII) — e.g., names/emails if users typed them in prompt. Rough estimate: window ~ 04:12:05 -> 04:20:12 UTC (about 8m). ~4k export events in that window.
sasha (security): please list potentially affected customers and confirm storage lifecycle. Is that telemetry S3 accessible externally or to other Google accounts? Any public ACLs?
alex (eng-sre): telemetry-prod S3 is internal, accessible only to telemetry service accounts and a small ops group. Retention policy is 24 hours; no public ACLs. We have 3 likely customer identifiers surfaced in the hashes that map to active accounts (mapping done locally): corp-a, devshop-inc, greenfield. Might be low-sensitivity but we need legal to weigh in.
morgan (pm): thanks. Carly, can you advise on notification requirements? Do we need a customer-facing disclosure? Also, status page update?
carly (legal): if there is any chance user-supplied content left unredacted in a telemetry export we should do a precautionary notification. Level depends on sensitivity and whether any identifying info was included. Please prepare a short 'potential exposure' notice for affected customers and a more generic status page update for everyone.
jamie (oncall): drafting status page update — pls review:
```text
Status: Investigating — possible inadvertent telemetry export
Details: A debug telemetry exporter was briefly enabled in our us-west-2 inference cluster, which may have recorded truncated request previews for a subset of requests between 04:12 and 04:20 UTC. We are investigating scope and have disabled the exporter. If you believe your data may be sensitive, contact support@redwood.ai. No evidence of external access.
Impact: Possible limited exposure of request prefixes (first ~128 chars) for a small fraction of requests. Mitigation: exporter disabled, data deletion requested from telemetry store.
Update: 04:25 UTC — exporter disabled, deletion requested. Further updates to follow.
```
liz (support): add guidance for customers to rotate any secrets if they believe they included them in prompts. We should proactively reach out to corp-a / devshop-inc / greenfield privately.
alex (eng-sre): mitigation steps executed:
1) disabled flag: `platformctl set-config inference.telemetry.debug_export false` (04:25:30 UTC)
2) revoked telemetry service write creds to telemetry-prod S3 (04:26:10 UTC)
3) issued deletion request to telemetry S3 path `s3://telemetry-prod/debug-exports/1851234567/*` (04:27:00 UTC)
Action logs show success responses from S3 delete job.
incident-bot: action-disable-telemetry-exporter completed at 1851234700 — status: success
jamie (oncall): confirmed disabled. alex, can you confirm counts and final scope so we can finalize messaging?
alex (eng-sre): final scope (post-collection): ~4,032 debug export objects, mapping to ~3 distinct customer account hashes. No downstream replication found beyond telemetry-prod S3. We scanned for copies and found none in long-term storage. Deletion job returned 200 and deletion markers present.
sasha (security): running a tighter scan for any unexpected IAM role access — no anomalies so far. Recommend initiating targeted outreach and offering rotation support + free incident review call.
carly (legal): proposed customer message (short):
```text
Subject: Potential telemetry export affecting request previews
Hello —
We are contacting you because we detected that a debug telemetry setting was briefly enabled in our us-west-2 inference service which may have captured truncated request previews (first ~128 characters) for a small set of requests during an approximately 8-minute window on DATE (04:12–04:20 UTC). We have disabled the exporter, requested deletion of the telemetry objects, and scoped the event to three customer accounts. There is currently no evidence of external access beyond our internal telemetry system. As a precaution, if you believe you included sensitive information (passwords, tokens, PII) in prompts during that time, please rotate those secrets and contact support@redwood.ai. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a post-incident report.
Regards,
Redwood Security & Support
```
morgan (pm): looks good. Action items: 1) targeted outreach to the three customers within 1 hour; 2) status page update (jamie posted); 3) security/forensics confirm deletion and access logs (sasha/alex) and prepare postmortem.
jamie (oncall): sending private outreach to account execs + support to trigger customer notifications now. cc: @liz for handoff. Also scheduling a 1pm postmortem convo and assigning to eng-runtime + security.
liz (support): outreach templates sent to account teams. Offering 1:1 triage and rotation help. Support ticket template created: `IN-1851234567`.
alex (eng-sre): follow-up — ran `aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket telemetry-prod --prefix debug-exports/1851234567/` and verified deletion markers. Saved audit logs to a locked bucket for legal review.
sasha (security): final note: no signs of external exfiltration. Recommend full postmortem and tightening of feature-flag gating (require two-person approval for telemetry exports). Adding to action items.
carly (legal): will draft the formal customer notice and advise on regulator disclosure if customers report sensitive data. For now proceed with targeted notices.
jamie (oncall): thanks team — incident declared mitigated, moving to monitoring. Filing for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
